# Load libraries and data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(countrycode)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(sf)
# Default image dimensions in inches and raster resolution.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, dpi = 144,
                      fig.align = "center")


data = read_csv("survey_11_11.csv")

data = data |> 
  select(-c(StartDate:Status), -c(RecordedDate:'Last Seen Question IDs'))

data = data[3:nrow(data), ]

```

# Question subtitles


```{r question-subtitles}
question_subtitles = c(
  discipline_of_interest = "",
  stage = "",
  ai_use = "How much do you currently use AI?",
  awareness = "Before reading the introduction above, how familiar were you with the recent reports of AI-generated mathematics research?",
  capability = "Within the next three years, what level of scientific research capability do you expect AI systems to achieve in your field?",
  displacement = "Advances in AI will significantly reduce the demand for human researchers in my field in the next three years.",
  threat = "Advances in AI threaten the continued existence and long-term viability of academic research as a human profession.",
  opportunity = "AI-driven research will increase the overall rate of scientific progress.",
  concern = "I am concerned about the implications of AI-driven scientific research for my own job security.",
  future = "How should you strategise about your work for the long term in light of recent AI developments?",
  ai_roles = "Highest level of AI autonomy you consider acceptable",
  change = "Have recent advances in AI-driven scientific research caused you to reconsider your research or academic career?",
  country = ""
)

question_subtitle = function(question, width = 85) {
  subtitle = unname(question_subtitles[question])
  if (length(subtitle) != 1 || is.na(subtitle) || !nzchar(trimws(subtitle))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  stringr::str_wrap(subtitle, width = width)
}

subtitle_height = function(subtitle) {
  if (is.null(subtitle)) return(0)
  0.22 * (stringr::str_count(subtitle, "\n") + 1) + 0.16
}
```

# Response order

```{r response-order}
agreement_order = c("Strongly disagree", "Somewhat disagree",
                    "Neither agree nor disagree", "Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree")

response_orders = list(
  displacement = agreement_order,
  threat = agreement_order,
  opportunity = agreement_order,
  concern = agreement_order,
  awareness = c("Not aware", "Heard about them, but know little",
                "Somewhat familiar", "Very familiar"),
  ai_use = c("Not at all",
             "I have only tried it occasionally",
             "I use it for a few specific tasks",
             "I regularly use it for some of my research tasks",
             "I use it for many of my research tasks",
             "It is integral to nearly all of my research work"),
  capability = c(
    "Cannot help researchers.",
    "Assist human researchers in carrying out research tasks.",
    "Perform research tasks independently, but produce lower-quality results than competent human researchers.",
    "Perform research tasks independently, producing results of comparable quality to those of competent human researchers.",
    "Perform research tasks independently, producing higher-quality results than competent human researchers."
  ),
  stage = c("PhD student", "Postdoctoral researcher", "Assistant professor",
            "Associate professor", "Full professor",
            "Currently not conducting research within an academic setting", "Other"),
  future = c("Yes (please describe how):", "I have no idea", "I don't want to answer"),
  change = c("I do not intend to reconsider my research or career.",
             "I am reconsidering research topics.",
             "I am increasing AI adoption in my research.",
             "I am reconsidering my academic career.",
             "I am considering sacrificing less of my life to science.",
             "I am considering training fewer researchers.",
             "Other", "I prefer not to answer.")
)
```

# Plot appearance and layout

```{r plot-helpers}
plot_base_size = 12
plot_label_size = 11

survey_theme = function(base_size = plot_base_size, infographic = FALSE) {
  ink = if (infographic) "#203044" else "#222222"
  background = if (infographic) "#FAF8F4" else "white"

  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = ink),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = background, color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = background, color = NA),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size + 4, face = "bold",
                                margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size, color = "#596675",
                                   margin = margin(b = 12)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = base_size),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.text = element_text(size = plot_label_size, color = ink),
      axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, lineheight = 1.05,
                                 margin = margin(r = 10)),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(size = plot_label_size),
      legend.text = element_text(size = plot_label_size),
      strip.text = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0,
                                  margin = margin(t = 10)),
      plot.margin = margin(16, 24, 16, 16)
    )
}

theme_academic = function(base_size = plot_base_size) {
  survey_theme(base_size)
}

theme_infographic = function(base_size = plot_base_size) {
  survey_theme(base_size, infographic = TRUE)
}

question_title = function(question) {
  titles = c(discipline_of_interest = "Discipline of interest",
             stage = "Career stage", ai_use = "AI use",
             role_ra = "AI as a research assistant",
             role_ir = "AI as an independent researcher",
             role_pr = "AI as a peer reviewer",
             role_je = "AI as a journal editor",
             role_gr = "AI as a grant reviewer",
             role_dm = "AI as a decision maker")
  if (question %in% names(titles)) unname(titles[question]) else
    stringr::str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", question))
}

category_plot = function(counts, title, percentage = FALSE,
                         infographic = FALSE, wrap_width = 32, subtitle = NULL,
                         response_order = NULL) {
  counts = counts |>
    mutate(response = as.character(response)) |>
    filter(!is.na(response), nzchar(trimws(response)))
  if (nrow(counts) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Never sort by count. Reverse levels because ggplot draws the first at bottom.
  if (is.null(response_order)) response_order = sort(unique(counts$response))
  unknown = setdiff(counts$response, response_order)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("Add these responses to response_orders: ", paste(unknown, collapse = "; "))
  }
  counts = counts |>
    tidyr::complete(response = response_order, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    mutate(value = if (percentage) n / sum(n) else n,
           label = if (percentage) scales::percent(value, accuracy = 1) else
             as.character(n),
           response = factor(response, levels = rev(response_order)))
  wrapped = stringr::str_wrap(levels(counts$response), width = wrap_width)
  # Reserve at least 0.42 inches per row, plus space for multiline labels.
  height = 1.8 + sum(pmax(0.42, 0.19 * (stringr::str_count(wrapped, "\n") + 1) + 0.16))

  p = ggplot(counts, aes(x = value, y = response)) +
    geom_col(fill = if (infographic) "#167D8D" else "#404B59", width = 0.68) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.2,
              size = plot_label_size / (72.27 / 25.4),
              color = if (infographic) "#203044" else "#222222") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = wrap_width)) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = if (percentage) scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1) else
        scales::label_number(accuracy = 1),
      breaks = if (percentage) scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5) else
        function(x) unique(round(scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)(x))),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
    ) +
    labs(title = stringr::str_wrap(title, width = 62),
         subtitle = subtitle,
         x = if (percentage) "Share of respondents" else "Number of respondents",
         y = NULL) +
    (if (infographic) theme_infographic() else theme_academic())
  attr(p, "figure_height") = max(4, height) + subtitle_height(subtitle)
  p
}

# Group comparisons: one complete response distribution per group.
grouped_ai_plot = function(data, question, group, group_order, group_title,
                            rank_responses = NULL) {
  answers = response_orders[[question]]
  if (is.null(answers)) stop("Missing response order for ", question)
  plot_data = data |>
    transmute(group = as.character(.data[[group]]),
              response = as.character(.data[[question]])) |>
    filter(!is.na(group), nzchar(trimws(group)),
           !is.na(response), nzchar(trimws(response)))
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) return(NULL)
  stopifnot(all(plot_data$response %in% answers),
            all(plot_data$group %in% group_order))
  groups = group_order[group_order %in% plot_data$group]
  # Rank using each group's valid answers, not raw response counts.
  # Ties retain the supplied discipline order.
  if (!is.null(rank_responses)) {
    stopifnot(all(rank_responses %in% answers))
    ranking = plot_data |>
      group_by(group) |>
      summarise(rank_share = mean(response %in% rank_responses), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(tie_order = match(group, groups)) |>
      arrange(desc(rank_share), tie_order)
    groups = ranking$group
  }
  diverging = identical(answers, agreement_order)

  segments = plot_data |>
    count(group, response) |>
    complete(group = groups, response = answers, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    mutate(response = factor(response, levels = answers)) |>
    arrange(group, response) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    mutate(total = sum(n), proportion = n / total,
           # Shift the whole stack so the neutral segment straddles zero.
           offset = if (diverging) sum(proportion[1:2]) + proportion[3] / 2 else 0,
           xmax = cumsum(proportion) - offset,
           xmin = xmax - proportion) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(y = match(group, rev(groups)),
           label = if_else(proportion >= if (diverging) 0.10 else 0.06,
                           scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 1), ""))
  stopifnot(all(abs(tapply(segments$proportion, segments$group, sum) - 1) < 1e-10),
            all(segments$xmax >= segments$xmin))

  if (diverging) {
    palette = c("#6A51A3", "#B6A2D5", "#F2D98D", "#7BC8B0", "#147D73")

  } else {
    # Viridis provides an ordered, colour-vision-friendly scale, yellow to purple.
    # A coloured light endpoint keeps "Not aware" visible against white.
    palette = viridisLite::viridis(length(answers), begin = 0.08, end = 0.90,
                                   direction = -1)
  }
  # Choose black or white text by the larger luminance contrast.
  rgb = grDevices::col2rgb(palette) / 255
  linear_rgb = ifelse(rgb <= 0.04045, rgb / 12.92, ((rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  luminance = colSums(linear_rgb * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
  text_colors = ifelse((1.05 / (luminance + 0.05)) > ((luminance + 0.05) / 0.05),
                       "white", "black")
  segments$text_color = text_colors[as.integer(segments$response)]
  legend_labels = if (question == "capability") {
    c("Cannot help researchers", "Assist human researchers",
      "Independent: lower-quality results", "Independent: comparable-quality results",
      "Independent: higher-quality results")
  } else answers
  legend_labels = stringr::str_wrap(legend_labels, width = 29)
  axis_labels = stringr::str_wrap(rev(groups), 31)
  subtitle = question_subtitle(question, width = 110)
  caption = if (diverging)
    "Disagreement left; agreement right; neutral centred on zero. Labels shown for segments >= 10%." else
    "Percentages within each group. Labels shown for segments >= 6%."
  caption = paste0(caption, "\nPercentages exclude missing answers to this question.")

  p = ggplot(segments) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = if (diverging) 0 else numeric(0),
               color = "#777777", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.40,
                  ymax = y + 0.40, fill = response), color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y, label = label, color = text_color),
              size = 10 / (72.27 / 25.4), show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(palette, answers), breaks = answers,
                      labels = legend_labels, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(groups), labels = axis_labels,
                       limits = c(0.35, length(groups) + 0.75),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = if (diverging) c(-1, 1) else c(0, 1),
                       breaks = if (diverging) seq(-1, 1, 0.25) else seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       labels = function(x) scales::percent(abs(x), accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(title = paste(question_title(question), "by", group_title),
         subtitle = subtitle, x = "Share of respondents within each group",
         y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = caption) +
    theme_academic() +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 12)),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 24), lineheight = 1.15),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 10, lineheight = 1.05),
          legend.key.width = grid::unit(15, "pt"),
          legend.key.height = grid::unit(12, "pt"),
          legend.margin = margin(t = 10, b = 6),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2))
  # Equal row spacing must accommodate the longest wrapped group label.
  row_height = max(0.85, max(stringr::str_count(axis_labels, "\n") + 1) * 0.20 + 0.22)
  # Reserve title/legend space separately so even two-group charts have thick bars.
  attr(p, "figure_height") = max(6, 3.5 + length(groups) * row_height + subtitle_height(subtitle))
  attr(p, "figure_width") = 12
  attr(p, "figure_label") = paste("grouped", group, question, sep = "-")
  p
}

grouped_plots = list()

# Child chunks give every plot in a loop its own device height when knitting.
show_survey_plot = function(p) {
  if (is.null(p)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (!isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) {
    print(p)
    return(invisible(p))
  }
  height = attr(p, "figure_height")
  width = attr(p, "figure_width")
  if (is.null(width)) width = 9
  label = attr(p, "figure_label")
  if (is.null(label)) label = ""
  output = knitr::knit_child(
    text = sprintf("```{r %s, echo=FALSE, fig.width=%.2f, fig.height=%.2f}\nprint(p)\n```",
                   label, width, height),
    envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE
  )
  cat(output, sep = "\n")
}
```

# Remove participants based on exclusion criteria

```{r}
data_filtered = data |> 
  filter(consent == "Yes",
         data_quality == "Yes",
         'Duration (in seconds)' >= 60,
         Progress == 100)
```

# Fix the questions

## Disciplines of interest

```{r}
data_filtered = data_filtered |>
  mutate(
    discipline_of_interest = case_when(
      discipline_1 == "Natural sciences" & discipline_2 == "Other natural sciences" ~ NA_character_,
      discipline_1 == "Natural sciences" ~ discipline_2,
      TRUE ~ discipline_1
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(discipline_of_interest))

# Natural-science fields first, then the other disciplines; alphabetical within each.
discipline_order = data_filtered |>
  distinct(discipline_1, discipline_of_interest) |>
  arrange(desc(discipline_1 == "Natural sciences"), discipline_of_interest) |>
  pull(discipline_of_interest) |>
  unique()
response_orders$discipline_of_interest = discipline_order
```

# Academic style

## Demographics

```{r academic-demographics, results='asis'}
for (question in demographics) {
  counts = data_filtered |> count(response = .data[[question]])
  show_survey_plot(category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question), infographic = FALSE,
    subtitle = question_subtitle(question),
    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  ))
}
```

## AI questions

```{r academic-ai, results='asis'}
for (question in ai_questions) {
  counts = data_filtered |> count(response = .data[[question]])
  show_survey_plot(category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question), infographic = FALSE,
    subtitle = question_subtitle(question),
    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  ))
}
```

## AI roles

Each panel shows the acceptable level of AI autonomy for one role. Percentages
use the non-missing responses for that role; panel headings report that sample
size. All panels share the same response order and percentage scale.

```{r academic-ai-roles, fig.width=12, fig.height=9 + subtitle_height(question_subtitle("ai_roles", width = 115))}
role_response_order = c("Not permitted", "Permitted with human supervision",
                        "Permitted autonomously", "Unsure")

role_responses = data_filtered |>
  select(all_of(names(ai_roles))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "role", values_to = "response") |>
  mutate(response = trimws(response)) |>
  filter(!is.na(response), nzchar(response))

# Fail visibly if the survey introduces an answer not covered by this ordering.
stopifnot(all(role_responses$response %in% role_response_order))

role_counts = role_responses |>
  mutate(role = factor(role, levels = names(ai_roles)),
         response = factor(response, levels = rev(role_response_order))) |>
  count(role, response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(role) |>
  mutate(total = sum(n),
         percentage = if_else(total > 0, n / total, NA_real_),
         value_label = if_else(total > 0,
                               scales::percent(percentage, accuracy = 1), "")) |>
  ungroup()

role_panels = role_counts |>
  distinct(role, total) |>
  mutate(heading = paste0(stringr::str_wrap(unname(ai_roles[as.character(role)]), 30),
                          "\n(n = ", total, ")"))
role_panel_labels = setNames(role_panels$heading, as.character(role_panels$role))

ai_roles_plot = ggplot(role_counts, aes(x = percentage, y = response)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#404B59", width = 0.65, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = value_label), hjust = -0.2,
            size = plot_label_size / (72.27 / 25.4), color = "#222222",
            na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(role), ncol = 2, drop = FALSE,
             labeller = labeller(role = role_panel_labels),
             axes = "all_y", axis.labels = "all_y") +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE,
                   labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 22)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.12), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(title = "Acceptable AI autonomy by role",
       subtitle = question_subtitle("ai_roles", width = 115),
       x = "Share of respondents within each role", y = NULL) +
  theme_academic() +
  theme(panel.spacing = grid::unit(18, "pt"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold",
                                   margin = margin(b = 10)))

ai_roles_plot
```

## AI questions by discipline

```{r ai-by-discipline, results='asis'}
# Descending positive agreement; awareness uses the most familiar response.
discipline_rank_responses = list(
  awareness = "Very familiar",
  displacement = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  threat = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  opportunity = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  concern = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree")
)
for (question in ai_questions) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "discipline_of_interest",
                      discipline_order, "discipline",
                      rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]])
  grouped_plots[[paste0("discipline_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```

## AI questions by familiarity, dichotomized

```{r ai-by-familiarity, results='asis'}
data_filtered = data_filtered |>
  mutate(awareness_dichotomized = case_when(
    awareness %in% c("Not aware", "Heard about them, but know little") ~
      "Not familiar",
    awareness %in% c("Somewhat familiar", "Very familiar") ~
      "Familiar",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Awareness defines these groups, so do not plot it against itself.
for (question in setdiff(ai_questions, "awareness")) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "awareness_dichotomized",
                      c("Not familiar", "Familiar"), "familiarity")
  grouped_plots[[paste0("familiarity_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```

## AI question pairs as heatmaps

All unique pairs of the six AI questions are shown once (15 panels).
Each cell is the percentage of respondents selecting that combination, among
those who answered both questions in that panel. The colour scale is shared
across panels; percentages within each panel sum to 100% before rounding.
Axes follow the response orders above, using abbreviated labels for readability.
AI roles remain separate from these questions.

```{r ai-pair-heatmaps, fig.width=18, fig.height=24, dpi=150, fig.retina=1}
# Short axis labels map to the exact survey answers in response_orders.
heatmap_response_labels = list(
  awareness = c("Not aware", "Heard about it;\nknow little",
                "Somewhat\nfamiliar", "Very familiar"),
  capability = c("Cannot help", "Assist humans", "Independent:\nlower\nquality",
                 "Independent:\ncomparable\nquality", "Independent:\nhigher\nquality"),
  future = c("Yes: describe how", "No idea", "Prefer not\nto answer")
)
for (question in c("displacement", "threat", "opportunity", "concern")) {
  heatmap_response_labels[[question]] = c(
    "Strongly\ndisagree", "Somewhat\ndisagree", "Neither agree\nnor disagree",
    "Somewhat\nagree", "Strongly\nagree"
  )
}
heatmap_label_lookup = unlist(lapply(ai_questions, function(question) {
  stopifnot(length(heatmap_response_labels[[question]]) == length(response_orders[[question]]))
  setNames(heatmap_response_labels[[question]],
           paste(question, seq_along(response_orders[[question]]), sep = "::"))
}))

ai_question_pairs = combn(ai_questions, 2, simplify = FALSE)
pair_heatmap_data = purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(ai_question_pairs), function(i) {
  pair = ai_question_pairs[[i]]
  row_question = pair[1]
  column_question = pair[2]
  row_answers = response_orders[[row_question]]
  column_answers = response_orders[[column_question]]
  paired = data_filtered |>
    transmute(row_answer = .data[[row_question]],
              column_answer = .data[[column_question]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(row_answer), nzchar(trimws(row_answer)),
           !is.na(column_answer), nzchar(trimws(column_answer)))
  stopifnot(all(paired$row_answer %in% row_answers),
            all(paired$column_answer %in% column_answers))
  paired |>
    count(row_answer, column_answer, name = "count") |>
    complete(row_answer = row_answers, column_answer = column_answers,
             fill = list(count = 0)) |>
    mutate(pair_id = i,
           panel = paste0(question_title(row_question), " (rows) / ",
                          question_title(column_question), " (columns)"),
           row_key = paste(row_question, match(row_answer, row_answers), sep = "::"),
           column_key = paste(column_question, match(column_answer, column_answers), sep = "::"),
           total = nrow(paired),
           proportion = if (nrow(paired) > 0) count / nrow(paired) else NA_real_)
})

# Unique keys allow each facet to retain its own semantic response order.
heatmap_keys = unlist(lapply(ai_questions, function(question) {
  paste(question, seq_along(response_orders[[question]]), sep = "::")
}))
pair_heatmap_data = pair_heatmap_data |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),
         row_key = factor(row_key, levels = rev(heatmap_keys)),
         column_key = factor(column_key, levels = heatmap_keys),
         cell_label = case_when(
           is.na(proportion) ~ "-",
           count == 0 ~ "0",
           proportion < 0.01 ~ "<1",
           TRUE ~ sprintf("%.0f", 100 * proportion)
         ))

pair_checks = pair_heatmap_data |>
  group_by(pair_id) |>
  summarise(total = first(total), cells = sum(count), share = sum(proportion), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(pair_checks) == choose(length(ai_questions), 2),
          all(pair_checks$cells == pair_checks$total),
          all(abs(pair_checks$share[pair_checks$total > 0] - 1) < 1e-10))

heatmap_max = max(c(0.01, pair_heatmap_data$proportion), na.rm = TRUE)
pair_heatmap_data = pair_heatmap_data |>
  mutate(text_colour = if_else(!is.na(proportion) & proportion > heatmap_max * 0.55,
                               "white", "#222222"))
ai_pairs_plot = ggplot(pair_heatmap_data,
                       aes(x = column_key, y = row_key, fill = proportion)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = cell_label, color = text_colour),
            size = 10 / (72.27 / 25.4), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F1F5F8", high = "#244E6A",
                      limits = c(0, heatmap_max), na.value = "#EEEEEE",
                      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                      name = "Share of paired responses") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) unname(heatmap_label_lookup[x]),
                   expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) unname(heatmap_label_lookup[x]),
                   expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 3, scales = "free",
             labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 42)) +
  labs(title = "AI questions: all pairwise response distributions",
       subtitle = "Rows and columns identify the two questions in each panel. Cell numbers are percentages of respondents answering both.",
       x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "One panel per unique pair; shared colour scale. Missing answers excluded separately for each pair.\n0 = no responses; <1 = less than 1%; - = no paired responses. Percentages may not sum to 100 after rounding.") +
  theme_academic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 1.05,
                                    margin = margin(t = 8)),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 1.05,
                                    margin = margin(r = 8)),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(24, "pt"),
        panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(30, "pt"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 12)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 20)),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2)) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = grid::unit(220, "pt"),
                               barheight = grid::unit(12, "pt"), title.position = "top"))

ai_pairs_plot
```


# Infographic style

## Demographics

```{r infographic-demographics, results='asis'}
for (question in demographics) {
  counts = data_filtered |> count(response = .data[[question]])
  show_survey_plot(category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question), percentage = TRUE, infographic = TRUE,
    subtitle = question_subtitle(question),
    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  ))
}
```

## World map

```{r world-map, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5 + subtitle_height(question_subtitle("country"))}
world = ne_countries(
  scale = "medium",
  returnclass = "sf"
)

world_data = world |>
  left_join(
    country_counts,
    by = c("adm0_a3" = "country_iso3")
  )

ggplot(world_data) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = n),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako",
    direction = -1,
    na.value = "grey90",
    name = "Participants"
  ) +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Geographical distribution of respondents",
    subtitle = question_subtitle("country")
  ) +
  theme_infographic() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth = grid::unit(100, "pt"),
    barheight = grid::unit(9, "pt"), title.position = "top"
  ))

country_check |>
  filter(!is.na(country_iso3)) |>
  anti_join(
    sf::st_drop_geometry(world),
    by = c("country_iso3" = "adm0_a3")
  )
```
